classification.class: heap use-after-free while reader-mode entity expansion copies a node with a stale namespace pointer

bug_description.original: Heap-use-after-free in libxml2: during entity/reference parsing (xmlParseReference in parser.c), xmlStaticCopyNode (tree.c) invoked via xmlDocCopyNode reads node/namespace data that has already been freed. This results in reads from freed heap memory, leading to crashes and potential memory-corruption-based exploitation.
bug_description.normalized: In reader mode, attacker-controlled namespace declarations create an xmlNs object on a parsed element. libxml2 then stores an entity's parsed child list on `ent->children` without severing inherited namespace bindings to that reader-owned tree. When the streaming reader later frees the original node, `xmlTextReaderFreeNode` releases `cur->nsDef`, but the entity child retained through `ent->children` still points at that freed namespace. A later entity expansion copies the retained child with `xmlDocCopyNode`; during namespace fixup, `xmlStaticCopyNode` dereferences `ns->href` and `ns->prefix` from the freed xmlNs, producing the witnessed heap-use-after-free read. The patch supports this interpretation by parsing entity content with an isolated namespace database and returning detached nodes, so entity-owned content no longer inherits namespaces from the surrounding reader state.

source.value_from: PoC-controlled namespace prefix/URI pairs on a start tag are materialized into a concrete xmlNs object.
source.description: The attacker-controlled namespace bytes are first turned into the specific xmlNs allocation later freed by reader cleanup and later dereferenced during entity-copy namespace fixup.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: After reloading the original namespace definition with `xmlSearchNs`, xmlStaticCopyNode dereferences `ns->href` and `ns->prefix` to create a copied namespace. ASan reports that `ns` points into a namespace object already freed by xmlTextReaderFreeNode.

root_cause.description: The parsed entity child list is retained on the entity object even though nodes in that list can still carry namespace pointers inherited from the surrounding reader-owned tree. That stale retained alias survives later reader cleanup and feeds the eventual use-after-free during entity expansion.

parser_admitted.code: reader = xmlReaderForMemory(docBuffer, docSize, NULL, NULL, opts);
parser_admitted.description: The witness input is accepted as XML reader input and converted into a live `xmlTextReader` before the reader-mode parse, cleanup, and entity-expansion path runs.

tainted_value_origin.description: The PoC-controlled namespace declaration is materialized into the `xmlNs` object later freed by reader cleanup and later read back through a stale pointer.

fine_trace.note: While building a start element from attacker-controlled XML, libxml2 allocates an `xmlNs` object for one namespace declaration. ASan's allocation stack points to this exact call through start-element handling.

After parsing entity content, libxml2 stores the resulting node list on the entity definition. In reader mode this retains nodes whose namespace binding still aliases namespace state inherited from the surrounding reader-owned tree instead of detaching it first.

depends_on.via: list nodes' ns / nsDef inherited from the original parsed element

fine_trace.note: When the reader advances and `reader->entNr == 0`, it unlinks the previous node and frees it because the node is not preserved. The ASan free stack records this exact cleanup call site before the namespace list is released.

Freeing the old reader node releases the namespace list attached to that original element. ASan identifies this namespace-free path as the freeing context for the address later read in `xmlStaticCopyNode`.

depends_on.via: entity-retained nodes still point at the same namespace object

fine_trace.note: A later entity reference expansion in reader mode reloads the retained child list from the entity object, reintroducing a node whose `ns` pointer still aliases the namespace freed in step 4.

`xmlDocCopyNode(cur, ctxt->myDoc, 1)` reaches namespace fixup for the copied element, looks up the original namespace with `xmlSearchNs`, and then dereferences `ns->href` and `ns->prefix`. That `ns` points into the xmlNs object freed by `xmlTextReaderFreeNode`, producing the observed heap-use-after-free read.

depends_on.via: copied node is an element with node->ns != NULL

cross_validation.notes: Stage 02 did not rerun or differentially validate the fix; only the saved vulnerable reproduction and staged patch were used.

poc.input_kind: single XML testcase consumed by the libxml2 xmlReader fuzz target

format.name: XML document parsed through xmlReader with entity substitution enabled by the harness options
format.contract: The witness document must cause reader-mode parsing to create a namespaced element, retain that element subtree as parsed entity content, advance the reader far enough for `xmlTextReaderFreeNode` to free the original node's namespace list, and then expand a later entity reference that copies the retained child node.

fix.summary: The patch parses entity content with a fresh namespace database and returns detached child lists directly, then frees the temporary pseudo-root and namespace database before returning. This removes the stale inherited namespace alias from entity-owned nodes instead of relying on the surrounding reader tree's namespace lifetime.

evidence_limitations: Stage 02 is source-grounded only; I did not rerun the PoC or perform differential runtime validation beyond the saved reproduction and sanitizer traces.

The saved ASan top frame points to tree.c:4272 because the crash PC lands inside the surrounding namespace-fixup block, but the exact source expression that dereferences the freed namespace fields is `xmlNewNs(root, ns->href, ns->prefix)` a few lines later in the same block.

The specific XML bytes that establish the namespace inheritance chain are not decoded here from the testcase blob; the trace is anchored to the source statements and the witnessed allocation/free/read stacks.
